_metadata.status: DRAFT — Requires domain expert validation before field deployment

runoff_coefficients._description: Runoff coefficient (C) for different roof surface types. Represents the fraction of rainfall that becomes runoff.
runoff_coefficients._source: IS 15797:2008 (Rainwater Harvesting, BIS), CGWB Manual on Artificial Recharge (2007), First Flush Diverter Standards
runoff_coefficients._note: ASSUMPTION — Values are representative ranges. Field verification recommended for precise sizing.

rcc_concrete.source: CGWB Master Plan for Artificial Recharge to Groundwater in India (2005), Table 3.2
rcc_concrete.applicability: Well-maintained RCC rooftop with no significant ponding or moss growth

corrugated_metal.source: IS 15797:2008, Central Ground Water Board documents
corrugated_metal.description: Corrugated Galvanized Iron (CGI) / Galvalume sheet roofing
corrugated_metal.applicability: Good condition metal sheets with proper slope

clay_tile.source: CGWB (2007), Ministry of Jal Shakti guidelines
clay_tile.applicability: Well-maintained clay tile roof; lower values for older/mossy tiles

asbestos_cement.applicability: Standard asbestos cement sheets; note health considerations for potable use

green_roof.applicability: Well-established vegetated roof system; highly variable

system_efficiency._description: Overall collection system efficiency accounting for first-flush losses, pipe losses, evaporation, and minor spillage.
system_efficiency.source: CGWB (2007), typical recommended practice for Indian conditions
system_efficiency.description: System collection efficiency for a properly designed RTRWH system including first-flush diverter, filter, and storage
system_efficiency.note: ASSUMPTION — Varies significantly with maintenance quality. Range: 0.70 to 0.95

first_flush_volume._description: Volume of initial runoff to be diverted as first-flush (contains maximum contamination from roof surface).
first_flush_volume.unit: mm of rainfall per unit roof area
first_flush_volume.source: IS 15797:2008 Clause 6; Ministry of Jal Shakti Jal Shakti Abhiyan guidelines
first_flush_volume.description: Recommended first-flush diverter volume: 2 mm equivalent of roof area per event
first_flush_volume.example: For 100 m² roof: 2 mm × 100 m² = 200 litres diverted per storm event
first_flush_volume.note: ASSUMPTION — May require adjustment based on local air quality and roof condition

recharge_structure_freeboard.source: General engineering practice for open-top recharge structures
recharge_structure_freeboard.description: Minimum freeboard to be maintained above maximum water level in recharge pit/trench

water_demand_per_capita._description: Per-capita daily water demand for different usage categories

domestic_urban.source: CPHEEO Manual on Water Supply and Treatment (2000), IS 1172:1993

soil_infiltration_rates._description: Indicative infiltration rates for different soil types. FIELD TESTING REQUIRED for design.
soil_infiltration_rates._source: CGWB Manual on Artificial Recharge (2007), Table 4.1
soil_infiltration_rates._warning: ASSUMPTION — These are representative values only. Percolation/infiltration test required for actual design.

gravel_coarse_sand.description: Gravel and coarse sand — very high infiltration

fine_sand.description: Fine to medium sand — high infiltration

black_cotton_soil.description: Expansive black cotton soil (Vertisol) — very low, problematic

recharge_pit.note: Depth limited to 3m for safety and construction practicality

recharge_trench.note: Gravel fill reduces effective storage volume by fill fraction

storage_tank.note: 10% freeboard allowance above calculated storage volume

recharge_shaft.note: Requires borehole drilling; depth depends on confining layers

disclaimer: All values in this configuration file are engineering assumptions based on standard references. They are intended for PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENT ONLY. Final design dimensions must be verified by a qualified engineer based on site-specific field investigations including: soil permeability testing, groundwater depth measurement, topographic survey, and structural assessment. This system does not replace professional engineering judgment.
